title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Pollard rho with cyclotomic squaring in GT

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, recover P in G1 with e(P,Q)=z under the pinned pairing convention. The algorithm in proof.md computes g=e(P0,Q) and solves z=g^a in GT by Pollard's three-way distinguished-point walk: cyclotomic squaring when the canonical residue modulo 3 is 0, dense multiplication by g when it is 1, and dense multiplication by z when it is 2. The walk state is an ordinary GT element. There is no Frobenius orbit and no representative selection. A distinguished-point collision yields the exponent a, or is rejected by the pinned pairing check. The algorithm stops after floor(1.2*sqrt(r)) steps or after ceil(11/16) of that many dense multiplications, whichever comes first, so the work is at most that many cyclotomic squarings and dense multiplications plus the one-time terms in proof.md. The attack uses at most 2^127.612559 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, restarts, verification and failures. Peak memory is at most 2^57.04 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^30 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Heuristic H1 in claim.json is the only nondeterministic premise. Success probability is at least 0.42.

experiments.purpose: On a toy prime-order additive group, run Pollard's three-way distinguished-point walk (double, add the generator, or add the target) and check that a collision recovers the secret. Doubling is the additive image of the cyclotomic squaring branch. This does not establish production field costs or the BLS pairing.
